thread:
lina: Heads-up team — org-level change rolling out tomorrow 09:00 UTC that affects how new service identities are provisioned. Please read and take action if you own infra or deployment tooling.

lina: TL;DR: We are enabling a new provisioning guardrail that enforces permission boundaries + ephemeral creds for service accounts created via our infra pipelines. Long-lived service account keys will be blocked for new accounts after enforcement. Existing long-lived keys must be rotated or marked for exemption. See the rollout plan below. :warning:

lina: Why: We've seen a steady increase in stale long-lived keys and cross-project broad roles. This reduces blast radius and makes short-lived credentials the default for programmatic access.

aj: Quick q — does this apply to Dedicated/Private customer-managed service identities?

lina: @aj it applies to Redwood org-managed identities and the internal infra project that runs our provisioning pipelines. Customer-managed identities (private deployments) are not changed, but we'll publish recommended modules to keep parity.

chen: Action items for infra teams?

lina: 1) Find service accounts with active user-managed keys and rotate them to workload-identity or short-lived tokens. 2) Update any automation that relies on downloading JSON keys to instead use OIDC/STS flows. 3) If you need an exemption (legacy on-call runbook), open an eng-security ticket with justification and expiry.

lina: Commands to list accounts with keys (GCP):
```
# list keys and ages
for sa in $(gcloud iam service-accounts list --format='value(email)'); do
  gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=$sa --format='table(name,validAfterTime,validBeforeTime)'
done
```

lina: AWS: find access keys older than 90 days: `aws iam list-access-keys --user-name ...` + use credential-report.

tom: For Terraform-managed service accounts, will the terraform module be updated to create permission boundaries automatically?

lina: Yes — we're shipping updated infra modules this afternoon. New module versions add a default permission boundary and an option to opt out (opt-out requires security ticket). Please pin to the new module v2.1.0 or later.

sarah: What about CI runners that still use JSON keys? We have a few legacy Jenkins jobs that do this.

lina: CI: migrate runners to short-lived credentials via workload identity federation or the credential helper. For Jenkins we have a migration doc: https://internal.redwood/infra/ci-migrate. If you have blockers, flag them here and tag infra-oncall.

infra-oncall-bot: @channel Reminder: automated audit will start at enforcement time and will create issues in the eng-security queue for noncompliant identities.

aj: Estimating impact — do we have a list of owners for service accounts?

lina: We're attaching the current ownership CSV to the eng-security ticket. If your team owns any service account without an owner in the CSV, please assign one by EOD tomorrow.

chen: Are there automated fallback/fail-open rules for critical infra during rollout?

lina: Yes: for the first 48 hours we have a soft-enforcement window — infra will log and open tickets. After 48h hard enforcement will block new key uploads and return 403 for attempted create-key operations. We also have rollback playbooks if a critical path is hit.

tom: Do we have an ETA on the TF module release? I can start pinning once I know the version.

lina: Module v2.1.0 releases at 16:00 UTC today. Changelog link: https://internal.redwood/infra/terraform-modules#service-account.

sarah: Noted. I'll start a sweep of Jenkins jobs and compile a list of ones that need migration.

aj: I'll coordinate with platform-auth to add examples for OIDC flows in our SDKs.

ops-bot: Deploy job 2245 finished: iam-guardrails:canary -> success (16:05 UTC) :white_check_mark:

lina: Thanks all. If you hit any immediate breakages after enforcement, ping @infra-oncall and add "iam-enforce-incident" to the ticket title. We'll keep a tight feedback loop and suspend enforcement if we see critical regressions.

chen: One last ask — can we get a short runbook on how to rotate a key safely (steps + smoke tests)?

lina: Yes — creating runbook now and will post linked in the ticket. Expected post time 17:00 UTC.

aj: Thanks — will re-audit our teams and follow up here. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall-bot: Audit note created: 48 service accounts flagged for manual review. Ticket: https://internal.redwood/engsec/tickets/RED-4123

lina: Closing the thread, will update the ticket with the runbook and module links. Enforcement: 2024-11-05T09:00:00Z (enforce start).
